metadata.title: Your Lab Data Gets Converted, Not Read.
metadata.topic: INSTRUMENT DATA TO ALLOTROPE · ANTHROPIC SKILL
metadata.purpose: Answer one real question in the Plain register: does Claude's instrument-data-to-Allotrope skill actually understand your lab results, or does it just reformat the file? Lands the carry-out that it detects the instrument and converts the file into one exact standard shape, the same way every time — it never interprets what the numbers mean.

beats.narration_text: Someone assumes this skill reads their lab data — understands it, judges it, the way a scientist would. It doesn't. It converts it, file by file, into one exact standard format.

beats.act: 1 anatomy — a skill is a folder
beats.narration_text: This conversion runs on something called a skill — a folder Claude reads before it works. Inside sit five files: a license, a requirements list, two supporting folders, and one instruction file, SKILL.md, that spells out exactly how a lab file becomes a standard record. Claude reads it, then follows it.

shot.new_visual_element: A folder icon opening to reveal SKILL.md, references/, scripts/; SKILL.md highlighted

production_viz.label: A skill is a folder
production_viz.mechanic: A folder opens on cream to reveal SKILL.md (highlighted in crimson), a references/ folder, a scripts/ folder. A caption below reads 'Claude reads it, then follows it.'

beats.narration_text: The steps run in order: read the file, work through each step exactly as written, then return the result. Nothing runs out of sequence unless a step itself says so.

production_viz.label: Input in, output out
production_viz.mechanic: Three cards left to right joined by arrows: 'Read SKILL.md', 'Execute steps in order', 'Return result'. Linear, no branch points drawn.

beats.act: 3 constraint — one job, two output shapes
beats.narration_text: For this skill there's one job: turn a lab instrument's output — PDF, CSV, Excel, or plain text — into one of two standard shapes: full Allotrope JSON, or a flattened CSV you can import anywhere. It figures out which instrument produced the file on its own. Ask it to interpret results or flag something scientifically odd, and there's no step written for that.

shot.new_visual_element: Four input formats converging through an auto-detect step into two output shapes; a boundary line captioned 'no interpretation past this line'

production_viz.label: One job, two output shapes
production_viz.mechanic: Four input chips (PDF, CSV, Excel, TXT) converge on an 'auto-detect instrument' node, which fans out to two output cards: 'Allotrope JSON' and 'Flattened CSV'. A dashed boundary line beneath, with a faint unlabelled field beyond it captioned 'no interpretation past this line'.

beats.narration_text: This skill doesn't interpret your lab results — it detects the instrument and converts the file into one exact standard shape, the same way every time.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt — read it with me. Ask Claude: I have a plain CSV export from a lab instrument, with columns like sample ID, measurement, units, and timestamp. Convert each row into one clean JSON record with consistent field names and ISO-format timestamps, and tell me the schema you used. Liam, in for Bear.
